title: runMaintenance fetches all memories via an empty FTS MATCH query, which SQLite rejects
body:
## Description

`MemoryManager.runMaintenance()` tries to load every stored memory so the retention policy can evaluate eviction candidates. It does so by calling the keyword search with an empty query string:

```ts
// packages/memory/src/memory-manager.ts:164-168
// Get all memories and evaluate retention
const allMemories = await this.memoryRepository.search("", 10000);
const evictionCandidates = this.retentionPolicy.getEvictionCandidates(allMemories);

const compactionResult = await this.compaction.compact(evictionCandidates.map((c) => c.entry));
```

The only concrete `MemoryRepository` is the SQLite adapter, whose `search` passes the query straight into an FTS5 `MATCH` clause with no empty-input guard:

```ts
// packages/infrastructure/src/database/sqlite.adapter.ts:154-165
async search(query: string, limit: number = 10): Promise<MemoryEntry[]> {
  const rows = this.db
    .prepare(`
      SELECT me.* FROM memory_entries me
      JOIN memory_entries_fts fts ON me.rowid = fts.rowid
      WHERE memory_entries_fts MATCH ?
      ORDER BY rank
      LIMIT ?
    `)
    .all(query, limit) as Record<string, unknown>[];
  return rows.map((r) => this.rowToEntry(r));
}
```

A `MATCH ''` (empty pattern) is not a valid FTS5 full-text query expression, so `better-sqlite3` throws `SqliteError: fts5: syntax error near ""` at the `.all(query, limit)` call. Note that the sibling `searchByEmbedding` does guard its degenerate input (`if (embedding.length === 0) return [];`, sqlite.adapter.ts:171), but `search` has no such guard.

## Impact

The entire maintenance cycle aborts with an exception before any compaction or retention enforcement runs. Memory compaction and tiered retention are therefore inoperative against the production (SQLite) backend: cold memories are never summarized or evicted, so the store grows without bound and the feature silently never works. Because the throw happens on the first line of real work in `runMaintenance`, any caller (scheduled job, manual trigger) fails every time. Justifies high severity: a core subsystem is completely non-functional and the failure is deterministic.

## Required Fix

1. Add a dedicated repository method to enumerate entries without FTS (e.g. `listAll(limit)` / `findAll(limit)` running `SELECT * FROM memory_entries ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?`) and call it from `runMaintenance` instead of `search("", ...)`.
2. Alternatively (or additionally), make `SQLiteMemoryRepository.search` short-circuit empty/whitespace-only queries by returning all rows (non-FTS query) or an empty array, matching the existing empty-input guard in `searchByEmbedding`.
3. Add a regression test that runs `runMaintenance()` against the SQLite adapter with stored entries and asserts it completes without throwing.

## References

- SQLite FTS5 full-text query syntax: https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html#full_text_query_syntax
- CWE-20: Improper Input Validation — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html

title: findNodesByLabel uses substring matching, merging unrelated nodes during graph extraction
getGraphContext passes the raw natural-language query to findNodesByLabel, so graph context is effectively never populated
mergeDuplicates/transferEdges creates duplicate edges with no de-duplication
search records access frequency but never updates accessedAt, so recency/decay scoring never reflects reads
CachedEmbeddingProvider evicts FIFO (not LRU) and performs no embedding-dimension validation
cosineSimilarity returns 0 for zero vectors and the default 0.0 threshold silently drops negative-similarity matches
In-memory vector and graph stores are unbounded, and compaction leaves orphaned vector entries in the index
indexBatch is O(n^2) due to repeated indexOf lookups
Pattern entity-extractor regex misses acronyms/non-ASCII and builds O(n^2) all-pairs relations
getNode mutates accessedAt on read, making reads non-idempotent and inconsistent with search
